tool.name: ValidateMetadata
tool.summary: Validates GeoTIFF files against product-specific requirements defined in TOML rule files.

usage.bullet_item: Validates GeoTIFF metadata (TIFF tags, GeoKeys, GDAL metadata, embedded XML) against configurable rules.
Supports batch validation of entire directories with optional name-based filtering.
Generates JSON summary reports with optional individual HTML or Markdown reports per file.
Files are labeled PASS or FAIL based on validation results in the output report filenames.
Custom validation rules can be defined in TOML files following the example_rules.toml format.

param.name: input_path
param.datatype: Raster Layer; Raster Dataset; File; Folder

P.SPAN: Select a GeoTIFF file, raster layer, or folder containing GeoTIFF files to validate. When a folder is selected, all .tif and .tiff files in the folder will be validated that contain the name filter (if used).
Directory containing TOML validation rule files. Defaults to gttk/resources/rules within the toolbox installation. Custom rules can be created following the format in example_rules.toml.

The product type to validate against (e.g., DGED5, GLO-30, NAIP). Product definitions are loaded from TOML files in the Rules Directory. Each product defines specific validation rules for TIFF tags, GeoKeys, GDAL metadata, and embedded XML.

Select which metadata sections to validate. Available sections: tag (TIFF tags), geokey (GeoKeys), gdal (GDAL_METADATA items and statistics), geo (GEO_METADATA embedded XML), xmp (XMP metadata), xml (external XML sidecar file), projjson (PROJJSON CRS). By default, all sections are validated.

Filter files by name when validating a directory. Only files containing this substring in their filename will be validated. Useful for mixed-product directories where files can be identified by naming convention.

Parent directory for the validation output folder. If not specified, the output folder is created alongside the input file or in the input directory. A timestamped subfolder (e.g., validation_20260117_120000) is automatically created.
When checked, individual HTML or Markdown reports are generated for each validated file in addition to the JSON summary. Report filenames include PASS or FAIL status (e.g., filename_PASS.html).
Format for individual validation reports. HTML provides formatted, styled reports suitable for viewing in web browsers. Markdown is plain text suitable for documentation and version control.
When checked, the JSON summary file will be automatically opened using the system's default application after validation completes.
The generated validation output folder containing the JSON summary and any individual reports. This path is automatically determined based on the input location and timestamp.
Path to the JSON summary file containing complete validation results for all processed files, including file metadata, validation status, and detailed rule-by-rule results.
